note.question: How should patient-specific medication regimen policies using wearable sensors in parkinson’s disease be optimized?
note.overview: Effective treatment of Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a continual challenge for healthcare providers, and providers can benefit from leveraging emerging technologies to supplement traditional clinic care. The paper develops a data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) framework to optimize PD medication regimens through wearable sensors. We leverage a data set of n = 26 PD patients who wore wrist-mounted movement trackers for two separate six-day periods.

source.quote: Effective treatment of Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a continual challenge for healthcare providers, and providers can benefit from leveraging emerging technologies to supplement traditional clinic care.
We develop a data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) framework to optimize PD medication regimens through wearable sensors.
We leverage a data set of n = 26 PD patients who wore wrist-mounted movement trackers for two separate six-day periods.
The results show that the RL-prescribed medication regimens outperform physicians’ medication regimens, despite physicians having access to the same data as the RL agent.

conditions: For CNN and LSTM, we test L2 regularization parameters λ ∈{0,0:01,0:1}.
Lastly, for all candidate models, we test Gaussian disturbance standard deviations σ ∈{0,0:5σ(r),σ(r)}, where σ(r) is the model’s residual standard deviation from training.

After selecting our final MDS-UPDRS-III symptom model, we use it to generate 100 MDS-UPDRS-III trajectories for our held-out test patients (i.e., the remaining 10% of patients from each fold who were not used for model selection) and evaluate the model’s MAE in predicting these patients’ average MDS-UPDRS-III scores and its AUC in predicting score improvement.

From the resulting 100 simulations, we define the PPMI patient’s “wearable-based RL regimen” as the RL-prescribed L-dopa regimen whose total LED is closest to the patient’s prescribed daily LED amount.
